{color:#bf2600}+*Scenario 1:*+{color}

* Go to Bolt3, hire a part-time worker _(no need to proxy as somebody specific)_, (50% FTE) in Malta and select any random date and month in 2024. 
* Then go to a new hire's profile, click on Actions > Time and Absence > Time Off Results by Period 
* Check the accrual on the first month, and check if the number is correct
** To calculate monthly accrual for the first month use the following formula:

8 hours (monthly accrual, due to 50% FTE) * number of calendar days EE worked this month / number of days in this month (30/31 days usually)

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Example*: 

* you hired EE on April 22nd 2024. An employee in the company with us for 8 days, meaning he gets accrual in April for 8 days. 
* Because the employee works *part*-time, they should accrue 8 hours per month 
* and in April we have 30 days
* 8 hours * 8 days / 30 ~ 2,13 hours = 2 hours will be accrued and shown in the report
{panel}

----

{color:#bf2600}+*Scenario 2:*+ {color}

* Go to Bolt3, hire a full-time worker _(no need to proxy as somebody specific)_, (100% FTE) in Malta and select any random date and month in 2024. 
* Then go to a new hire's profile, click on Actions > Time and Absence > Time Off Results by Period 
* Check the accrual on the first month, and check if the number is correct
** To calculate monthly accrual for the first month use the following formula:

16 hours (monthly accrual, due to 100% FTE) * number of calendar days EE worked this month / number of days in this month (30/31 days usually)

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Example*: 

* you hired EE on April 22nd 2024. An employee in the company with us for 8 days, meaning he gets accrual in April for 8 days. 
* Because the employee works *full*-time, they should accrue 16 hours per month 
* and in April we have 30 days
* 16 hours * 8 days / 30 ~ 4,12 hours = 4 hours will be accrued and shown in the report
{panel}

----

{color:#bf2600}+*Scenario 3:*+{color}

Find someone in Malta who is already working at Bolt, add a vacation in a random month in 2024 and then offboard them the same month. (Example: time off request for July, 1 week = 40 hours and then offboard at the end of July)

Once offboarding is complete, make sure to check the termination adjustment _(to check that go to the employee’s profile > Actions > Time and Absence > Maintain Accrual and Time Off Adjustments/Overrides > Termination Adjustments Tab)_

Then run the report ‘Time Off Results by Period’ in the column ‘Time Off Paid Year to Date’ should be a total number of hours requested for time off + hours from termination adjustments 

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Example:*

Employee was offboarded on May 15th 2024

In 2024 employee worked 5 months:

January, February, March, April – 16 hours accrued per month * 4 = 64 hours

May (14 days employee was in the company) = 7 hours 

Total accrued = 71 hours in total - X hours that was requested for vacation, for example 40 hours = 31 hours remaining and it should appear in the Termination Adjustments
{panel}

The plastic detail has heated (sunlight, internal high temperature) and expanded. Since it is riveted from four corners, the only way to go is upwards where there is no resistance.

For existing situations, our only options are to:

* Remove the plastic, clean all sealant and apply a new one, refit the existing plastic with rivets. 
** The plastic will still expand/shrink from temperature, but sealant is not too difficult to add/clean. Plastic will still deform eventually and will need replacement.
* Remove the plastic, clean all sealant, apply new plastic piece with rivets
** Slightly more expensive, plastic will still deform eventually and will need replacement.

To improve the design:

* Consider adding extra fasteners in the middle area, so the plastic would be attached to the frame more snugly, avoiding expansion which would tear away from the sealant.
** 2 rivets on each side (similar to existing ones) would do. With a single rivet in the middle the edges would still pry upwards and the sealant would fail. If only the center part expanded slightly, it would not be a problem.
** During the replacement/repair, these holes can be drilled to the frame.

There are two options to solve this:

* Instead of BOM uses a PC sheet, rivet it as it’s done today
* Non-riveted plate glued with Tinitrol 410

Regarding the charger lifetime estimation - Delta applies load to the chargers on room temperature and they measure capacitor parameters after known amount of work time of the capacitors.

After that they measure the capacitor parameters (ESR, capacitance) and estimate the lifetime based on calculations.

They do this evaluation based on electrolytic aluminum capacitors because these are the components with shortest lifetime.

What I suggest we do:

* *Specify from manufacturer the expected lifetime of the charger*:
** Working hours (idle & charging)
** Maximum charging cycles (based on charging a Cobra battery for 42V and OKAI battery for 54V)
** Absolute MAX. operating temperature
* *Test conditions*
** Test the charging in the extreme conditions - Accelerated Lifetime Testing (abbreviation - *ALT from now*).
** Find a standard which can apply to this test - Mr. [~accountid:6215e9f275803500683497d5]  to check with Delta - they do these types of tests.
** Create a test-setup compliant to the standard and acquire necessary tools/instruments for measuring results.
* *Outcome*
** Find out whether the Gojusin 42V and 54V chargers withstand the ALT and thus test the lifecycle and performance of the charger.
** Charger must work throughout and after the test - performance of the charger should not degrade significantly.
** Monitor charger behavior during the test (deviations, extremes)
*** Power consumption (input current, voltage, power etc.)

Conclusion - it`s not functioning as a steerer vertical tilting angle (vertical angle viewed from the front of the dock) limiter on Bolt 4, ES400B, ES600 and EB100B. On Bolt 4 and ES400B the space is too big. Plastic part of the socket functions as the angle limiter and steerers of the scooter doesn`t reach to the metal guide in this case. On ES600 the sheet metal is too flexible. It doesn`t function as tilting angle limiter in this way. The concept requires improvement. It definitely provides value on EB100B - if the steerer is turned on the left or right and if the guide is not used and if the locking mechanism is not used, the bike might fall off from the slot because of the mass of the bike. It`s possible to place the bike charging under an angle which might damage the adapter or inner parts of the slot if the guide is not used. The guide helps to prevent the bikes from getting the handlebar turned left and right. [https://taxify.atlassian.net/l/c/Mv4wNr25|https://taxify.atlassian.net/l/c/Mv4wNr25|smart-link]

In Germany there is a regulation that specifically adresses charging docks (Ladesäulenverordnung) but this is applicable only for cars. There is no regulation applicable to charging stations specifically for scooters or bicycles.The Länder (e.g. states) have separate regulation on how and what may be constructed on public ground (Bauordnungsrecht), however most Länder (Baden-Württemberg, Bremen, Hessen, Niedersachsen, Rheinland-Pfalz, Saarland, Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt und Schleswig-Holstein) have already exempted (car) charging infrastructure from this, meaning one does not need to adhere to these state regulations. The other states also predominantly do not require permission according to this construction law for charging points. All of these do not explicitly apply to E-Scooter charging docks however, as this is a completely new type. There is no specific regulation for this, meaning it is likely a legal gray area to date.

EMC tests were performed by 04/10 as one day (10:00 to 18:30)

Conducted and Radiated Emission & Immunity tests were performed under industrial and residential environmental standard scopes.
ESCS2 passed through the majority of the tests regarding the EMC emissions and immunity tests. Failed two specific tests of the residential environments scope that we are targeting to be compliant.

*Immunity against conducted disturbances test failed: ESCS2 charging slots communication interrupted (stopped charging) in certain frequency or frequency bands for both industrial and environmental standards, yet ESCS2 was able to recover itself after the certain frequency band disturbance is changed to another frequency, which was a good sign and acceptable for another level of compliance (drop level A to B can be understood better with the test report descriptions). Therefore, it was advised by the LEITC professionals that we shall indicate that disturbance may give cause interruptions to the functionality of the product specifications which will be enough, and no further effort is needed for this case.

*Radiated emission test failed for residential environment standards (pass on industrial): The root cause of the failure might be the RFID harmonics and RFID cable / the RFID board power calibration according [~accountid:5fc10e1e2730d80076c1d3a4]. That is being investigated already. Power regulating software is going to be tested. This test will be performed again in LEITC, 19/10 and 20/10 is booked (as per the LVD tests finishing date). Updated software should be tested and ready before going to LEITC again.

As per the discussion and agreement with LEITC, we can go and perform *only failed tests* again (following the LVD tests in TUV LV), and those will be added to the conformity report so that we don’t have to perform the entire test scope one more time, as long as we don’t have changes on the hardware.

In conclusion, EMC tests will be repeated for only Conducted Emission test with the full 10-slot assembly, date is booked yet will be confirmed as per the LVD finishing date.

*TLDR:* According to EMCD (Directive 2014/30/EU) The ESCS2 has to be certified as 1 product - the Whole rack has to be tested for EMC

The conclusions that Mr Erdi made are wrong. EMCD directive defines different installation cases. 

ESCS2 is NOT a fixed installation.

Examples of fixed installations: 
Industrial plants, power plants, power supply networks, telecommunication networks, cable TV networks, computer networks, airport luggage handling installations, airport runway lighting installations, automatic warehouses, skating hall ice rink machinery installations, storm surge barrier installations (with the control room etc.), wind turbine stations, car assembly plants, water pumping stations, water treatment plants, railway infrastructures, air conditioning installations.

RED Refers to EMCD (Directive 2014/30/EU) in which the different kind of apparatus is defined.

According to Guide for the EMCD (Directive 2014/30/EU) ESCS2 is a “combination of Finished products”

1.5.2 Combination of finished products Under the EMCD, a combination of several finished products is considered to be apparatus27 if: 

 is made available by an economic operator as a single functional unit;  intended for the end-user to be operated together to perform a specific task; and  is liable to generate electromagnetic disturbance or the performance of which is liable to be affected by such disturbance

*Such a combination, within the sense of the EMCD, is a single apparatus and all provisions of the EMCD apply to the combination as a whole (including the requirements on CE Marking, contact details etc.).* 

*Combining two or more CE marked finished appliances does not automatically produce a “compliant” system* e.g.: a combination of CE marked Programmable Logic Controllers and motor drives may fail to meet the essential requirements.



RFID and IoT are Sub components which are not installed by “end user” (Customer that inserts the scooter into the dock), therefore they do not need separate RED certification.

[DocsRoom - European Commission (europa.eu)|https://ec.europa.eu/docsroom/documents/33162]

”*1.6.3.11 Fixed Installations*
{color:#ff5630}*Fixed installations are not regulated under the RED*{color}. Since it is relevant in certain cases (through the link to the EMCD in Article 3.1.b), a distinction is made between two types of installations that are fixed. These are described below:

* Fixed installations as defined and described in the EMCD, i.e., which are unique in their build-up;
* Installations built up of mass-market equipment but are fixed in the sense that they are permanent in their place.

*Installations built up of mass-market equipment but are fixed in the sense that they are* {color:#ff5630}*permanent in their place*{color}
Regarding radio equipment intended for inclusion in non-specific installations, Article 17.1 of the RED requires that “conformity assessment shall take into account all intended operating conditions and, for *the essential requirement set out in Article 3.1.a*, the assessment shall also take into account the reasonably foreseeable conditions of use. Where applicable these conditions may, w*hen putting radio equipment into service, include combining the radio equipment with other equipment to form an installation that is fixed at its location.*
Considering the types of equipment that are likely to be included in such installations, the installation instructions of the radio equipment should describe how to install the equipment to enable it to operate as foreseen and if needed, what type of components shall be used. It is then for the legal or private person, who is responsible for putting into service or use of radio equipment, to *ensure that radio equipment is properly installed, maintained, and used for its intended purpose.”*



*Supplementary Guidance on the LVD/EMCD/RED*
[Supplementary guidance on EMC, LVD and RED (beama.org.uk)|https://www.beama.org.uk/static/uploaded/316d0e9b-83ed-4408-a285b048e0ad8a58.pdf]

{color:#ff5630}*“2*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}{color:#ff5630}*Non-radio electrical products functioning with radio equipment*{color}
{color:#ff5630}Electrical or electronic products whose function is not{color} to intentionally emit or receive radio waves for the purpose of {color:#ff5630}radio communication and/or radiodetermination{color} (in this section referred to as 'non-radio product') {color:#ff5630}may function with radio equipment.{color}

The RED is applicable to the combination of the radio equipment and the non-radio product as a whole only if the radio equipment is:

* incorporated into the non-radio product; and
* permanently affixed to the non-radio product.

Hence if the radio equipment is incorporated in a fixed and permanent way in the non-radio product at the moment of its placing on the EU market (i.e. in such a way that it cannot be easily accessed and readily removed), as specified above, this product is deemed to be a single product.
{color:#ff5630}*In the other cases the radio equipment and the non-radio product are considered as separate finished products and only the radio equipment is subject to the RED.”*{color}

In conclusion as per the “RED Guide” and “Supplementary Guidance on the LVD/EMCD/RED”, ESCS2 is not subject to the RED, because:

# It is a fixed installation to a permanent location and,
# Its radio equipment is not permanently fixed to the non-radio equipment and only radio equipment is subject to the RED. 

So IoT box and RFID boards shall be assessed separately as radio equipment, rather than full ESCS2 assembly.”
